question: What is the primary location of smooth muscle tissue in the human body?
explanation: Smooth muscle is found within the walls of hollow organs like blood vessels and the digestive tract to regulate internal movement. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h1)

question: Which muscle tissue type is under conscious somatic control?
explanation: Skeletal muscle attaches to bones and is controlled voluntarily through the somatic nervous system for body movement. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h1)

question: What name is given to the specialized plasma membrane of a skeletal muscle fiber?
explanation: The sarcolemma is the cell membrane of a striated muscle fiber responsible for conducting action potentials. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h2)

question: What is the primary function of T-tubules in a skeletal muscle fiber?

options.A: Carrying electrical impulses deep into the muscle cell
options.B: Providing oxygen storage directly to myofibrils
options.C: Storing large amounts of resting calcium ions
options.D: Synthesizing new actin and myosin protein strands

explanation: T-tubules allow surface action potentials to penetrate rapidly into the interior of the muscle fiber. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h2)

question: Which neurotransmitter is released at the neuromuscular junction to stimulate muscle contraction?
explanation: Acetylcholine is the primary neurotransmitter used at the neuromuscular junction to cross the synaptic cleft and stimulate the muscle fiber. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h3)

question: What chemical event immediately follows acetylcholine binding to receptors on the motor end plate?

options.A: Potassium ions flood into the synaptic cleft
options.B: Myosin heads detach completely from actin
options.C: Calcium ions are pumped into the T-tubules
options.D: Sodium ions rush into the muscle fiber

explanation: Binding opens ligand-gated channels, letting sodium rush inward to depolarize the motor end plate. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h3)

question: What cellular structure stores and releases calcium ions during muscle excitation?
explanation: The sarcoplasmic reticulum acts as a specialized calcium reservoir inside the muscle fiber. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h4)

question: How does the action potential reach the interior of the muscle fiber to release calcium?
explanation: T-tubules conduct the surface electrical signal deep into the muscle fiber interior to trigger calcium release. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h4)

question: Which regulatory protein does calcium bind to during the initiation of contraction?
explanation: Calcium binds to troponin, causing a shape change that shifts tropomyosin away from the active binding sites. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is the primary function of tropomyosin in a resting skeletal muscle fiber?

options.A: Cleaving ATP molecules to release chemical energy
options.B: Providing structural support to the Z-line
options.C: Pumping calcium ions back into storage vesicles
options.D: Blocking myosin binding sites on actin filaments

explanation: Tropomyosin covers the active sites on actin during rest to prevent unwanted muscle contraction. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h5)

question: What molecule must bind to the myosin head to cause it to detach from actin?
explanation: Binding of a new ATP molecule is required for the myosin head to release its grip on the actin filament. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h6)

question: What happens to the length of individual actin and myosin filaments during contraction?

options.A: They elongate to bridge the expanding Z-lines
options.B: They shorten significantly as the sarcomere contracts
options.C: They dissolve completely into individual amino acids
options.D: They remain the same length while sliding past each other

explanation: Filaments do not change length during contraction; they slide past one another to shorten the sarcomere. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h6)

question: Which enzyme breaks down acetylcholine in the synaptic cleft to stop muscle stimulation?
explanation: Acetylcholinesterase rapidly degrades acetylcholine in the synapse to halt ongoing neuromuscular stimulation. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h7)

question: Why is cellular energy (ATP) required for muscle relaxation?

options.A: To break down remaining actin filaments in the sarcoplasm
options.B: To push T-tubules back to their original resting surface length
options.C: To actively pump calcium ions back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum
options.D: To synthesize new acetylcholine molecules inside the motor neuron

explanation: Active transport pumps require ATP to move calcium ions against their concentration gradient back into storage. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h7)
